reading.body:
The US Department of Energy's Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory reported that data centers consumed about 4.4 percent of US electricity in 2023, and projected that share to reach 6.7 to 12 percent by 2028, naming AI as the driver of that increase.

NVIDIA's GB200 NVL72 rack system is cited as the forcing function behind a broader liquid cooling transition, since 120-kilowatt-class racks ended air cooling's viability at the AI high end, a specific figure that lines up with the rack density thresholds tracked elsewhere in this site's data center metrics, where cooling above roughly 30 kilowatts per rack already exceeds what air cooling can reliably remove. Google's own disclosed fleet-wide Power Usage Effectiveness, a trailing twelve-month figure near 1.1, is offered as the reference efficiency disclosure in this collection, the same figure this site's power efficiency metric describes as the level large modern hyperscale facilities report.

Only three items make up this collection, a federal demand projection, one hardware-driven cooling transition, and one company's efficiency disclosure, which is a narrow evidentiary base for a topic, data center power and cooling, that this entire site treats as the binding constraint on AI scaling.
